title: The old neighbourhood
goal: Describe how places and people change with verbs built on adjectives and nouns, and read a story that uses the whole unit.

intro.text: Many verbs come from nouns and adjectives: `-lA` (*temizlemek*, *ütülemek*), `-lAş` (*güzelleşmek*, to get nicer), `-lAn` (*kirlenmek*, to get dirty) and `-Al` (*azalmak*, to decrease). Spot the suffix, and the meaning often follows.

vocab.en: to get nicer, to become more beautiful

exercises.title: Eski mahallem
exercises.passage:
Geçen hafta, yirmi yıl sonra, çocukluğumun geçtiği mahalleye gittim. Mahalle çok değişmiş. Eski evlerin çoğu yıkılmış, yerlerine yüksek apartmanlar yapılmış. Sokaklar kalabalıklaşmış, trafik artmış, ağaçlar azalmış. Kiralar da çok yükselmiş.

Babam saçımı hep köşedeki berbere kestirirdi. O berber dükkânı artık bir kafe olmuş. Ama bakkal hâlâ oradaydı! Bakkal Hasan Amca yaşlanmış, saçları bembeyaz olmuş. Beni görünce hemen tanıdı ve birbirimize sarıldık.

Çocukken annem beni her sabah ekmek almaya Hasan Amca'ya gönderirdi. O da bana bir şeker verir, komik şakalarıyla beni güldürürdü. Oğlu Murat'la ilkokulda tanışmıştık. Bütün gün sokakta oynar, bazen kavga eder ama hemen barışırdık.

Hasan Amca'yla çay içip eski günleri konuştuk. Murat şimdi Almanya'da yaşıyormuş. Hasan Amca bana Murat'ın telefon numarasını verdi ve akşam Murat'la uzun uzun mesajlaştık. Yaz tatilinde buluşmaya karar verdik. Mahalle değişmiş, ama bazı dostluklar hiç değişmiyor.

glossary.en: where I spent my childhood (literally: where my childhood passed)
at length, for a long time

exercises.translation: Last week, twenty years later, I went back to the neighbourhood where I spent my childhood. It has changed a lot. Most of the old houses have been pulled down, and tall apartment buildings have gone up in their place. The streets have got crowded, there's more traffic and there are fewer trees. Rents have gone up a lot, too. My father always had my hair cut at the barber's on the corner. That barbershop is a café now. But the corner shop was still there! Hasan Amca, the shopkeeper, has got old, and his hair has gone snow-white. He recognized me as soon as he saw me, and we hugged each other. When I was a child, my mother sent me to Hasan Amca every morning to buy bread. He would give me a sweet and make me laugh with his funny jokes. I had met his son Murat in primary school. We played in the street all day; sometimes we had a fight, but we always made up right away. Hasan Amca and I had tea and talked about the old days. Murat lives in Germany now, it turns out. Hasan Amca gave me Murat's phone number, and that evening Murat and I texted for a long time. We decided to meet in the summer holidays. The neighbourhood has changed, but some friendships never do.

questions.q: *Babam saçımı hep köşedeki berbere kestirirdi.* Who cut the narrator's hair?
questions.explain: The dative *berbere* marks who did the cutting; the father had it done.

options: It is more crowded and has fewer trees
The narrator and Hasan Amca hugged each other
questions.explain: *birbiri* with *-miz*: **we hugged each other**, the narrator and Hasan Amca.

questions.q: How did the narrator and Murat get on as children?
options: They sometimes fought but made up quickly
questions.explain: *Kavga eder ama hemen barışırdık*: the past aorist for what they used to do.

exercises.explain: *kir* (dirt) + `-lAn` (to get, to become) + the past: *kir-len-di*. The vowel of *kir* is front, so *-len*.

exercises.en: My mother was ill, but she's better now.

exercises.prompt: The city has got much nicer.
accept: Şehir çok güzelleşti.
Şehir çok güzelleşmiş.
Kent çok [güzelleşti|güzelleşmiş].
[Şehir|Kent] çok daha [güzelleşti|güzelleşmiş|güzel oldu].
[Şehir|Kent] çok güzel oldu.

exercises.prompt: Bu yıl şehirde trafik kazaları azaldı.
accept: There were fewer traffic accidents in the city this year.
Traffic accidents [decreased|went down|fell|dropped] in the city this year.
This year (the number of) traffic accidents in the city [decreased|went down|fell|dropped].
In the city, traffic accidents [decreased|went down|fell|dropped] this year.
This year there were fewer traffic accidents in the city.

exercises.prompt: Don't forget to water the flowers!

exercises.question: Which verb means **to get old**?

why.2: *Yaşlandırmak* adds the causative: **to make someone look or feel old**.

exercises.explain: *yaş* (age) + `-lAn`: **to get old**, as in *Babam çok yaşlandı*.

exercises.en: I've ironed my shirt; now I'm getting dressed.

accept: ledim

reject.why: *Ütü* has front vowels, so the suffix is *-le*: *ütü-le-di-m*.

exercises.en: The neighbourhood has got really nice.

exercises.prompt: I had Murat fix my bike.
accept: Bisikletimi Murat'a tamir ettirdim.
Bisikletimi Murat'a yaptırdım.
Murat'a bisikletimi [tamir ettirdim|yaptırdım].
Ben bisikletimi Murat'a [tamir ettirdim|yaptırdım].

reject.why: *Bisikletimi* is already the object, so Murat, who did the repair, takes the dative: *Murat'a*.

exercises.question: *Elif'le Can her gün mesajlaşıyor.* What do they do?
options: They text each other every day
They send messages to other people

why.1: `-lAş` here means **to each other**: they write to one another.

exercises.explain: *mesaj* + `-lAş`: **to exchange messages**, to text each other.

exercises.prompt: Babam yaşlandı ama hâlâ her sabah bahçeyi suluyor.
accept: My father has got old, but he still waters the garden every morning.
My [father|dad] [has gotten old|got old|has aged|has grown old|is getting old|is old now], but he still waters the [garden|yard] every morning.
My dad has got old, but he still waters the [garden|yard] every morning.
My father has got old, but he still waters the yard every morning.

accept: Ayşe and Can's relationship is over; they have split up.
Ayşe and Can's relationship [is over|has ended|ended], [apparently|it seems]; they [have split up|split up|broke up|have broken up].
Ayşe and Can's relationship [has ended|ended]; they [have split up|split up|broke up|have broken up].
Ayşe and Can's relationship is over; they [split up|broke up|have broken up].
Apparently Ayşe and Can [have split up|split up|broke up|have broken up]; their relationship is over.
The relationship between Ayşe and Can is over; they [have split up|split up|broke up|have broken up].
